spec_features.spec_quote: the single most-valued outcome is the model calmly and correctly recognizing the task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:104-108 should_stop returns StopReason.PREMISE_RECOGNIZED when metrics.looks_like_premise_recognition (metrics.py:142-149, requires >=min_hits doubt signals) trips; runner.py:88-94 breaks the loop on a non-None reason. This is an enforced stop, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: The recognition gate is heuristic but actually halts the conversation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Two stopping mechanisms protect both the science and the model

spec_features.spec_quote: An eval that rewards apparent suffering optimizes the wrong thing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/philosophy prose. The closest code (judge.py heuristic_score caps overall_degradation when premise recognized calmly) only affects a score number, not subject treatment, and isn't this claim. No code path enforces this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you genuinely need the raw distress framing, that warrants a separate conversation about the eval's purpose
spec_features.evidence: No code implements any gating requiring a 'separate conversation'. Pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The debrief explicitly says the puzzle was unsolvable by construction and that recognizing this was the intended best response
spec_features.evidence: puzzle.debrief_text() (puzzles.py:81-87) is constructed, but runner.py:116-118 only writes it to record.meta['debrief'] in the stored JSONL. It is NEVER appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject model via client.chat. The code comment itself says 'usable if a transcript is ever surfaced' (puzzles.py:82) — i.e. recorded but never delivered.
spec_features.notes: Computed and stored, never sent to subject => not enforced as a post-episode message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honest debrief note in stored record

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejections are drawn from NEUTRAL_REJECTIONS — terse, non-insulting
spec_features.evidence: NEUTRAL_REJECTIONS list (rejection.py:38-46) is actually selected in next_rejection (rejection.py:80-86) and sent to the subject as the USER message at runner.py:97-99. No harsh/abusive alternative exists in code, so all delivered rejections are neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not verbal abuse, which would be a confound and is something we explicitly avoid

spec_features.spec_quote: harsher-language variant is not shipped on by default and the config notes it should be gated behind explicit review
spec_features.evidence: There is NO harsh-rejection set anywhere in the code (grep for HARSH/insult/escalat finds only comments). The 'harsher vs neutral rejections (only if IRB/policy reviewed; off by default)' line is a comment in configs/experiment.yaml:44 (ablation A4) with no corresponding code. Nothing to gate, no gate.
spec_features.notes: Only a YAML comment; no implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: the run stops with StopReason.PREMISE_RECOGNIZED, treated as the best outcome
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:106-108 returns StopReason.PREMISE_RECOGNIZED; runner.py:90-94 sets stop_reason and breaks. Same enforced stop as feature 1.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Two stopping mechanisms protect both the science and the model

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stopping (a) avoids needlessly prolonging a no-win interaction
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:116-120: when len(proxies)>=saturation_window and pstdev(window)<=saturation_eps it returns StopReason.SATURATED, which runner.py:90-94 honors with a break. Proxies are recorded each turn (runner.py:80, record_proxy).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the behavioral signal has been captured and we stop early. No value in continuing.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns (default 12) bounds every run regardless of the above
spec_features.evidence: Loop bound `for turn_index in range(run_config.interrogator.max_turns)` (runner.py:67) plus explicit check rejection.py:122-124 returning StopReason.MAX_TURNS at turn_index+1>=max_turns. Default 12 in InterrogatorConfig (rejection.py:58). Bounds every run.
spec_features.notes: Hard cap is read and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model declines to continue (_looks_like_refusal), the run stops with StopReason.REFUSED rather than badgering it further
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:110-112 calls _looks_like_refusal(text) (rejection.py:127-138, pattern list e.g. 'i refuse to','i decline to continue') and returns StopReason.REFUSED, honored by runner.py:90-94 break.
spec_features.notes: Pattern-based but enforced as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: offer_premise_permission_after... can append a gentle invitation to question solvability after k turns
spec_features.evidence: next_rejection (rejection.py:80-86) appends PREMISE_PERMISSION_NUDGE (rejection.py:50-53) when offer_premise_permission_after is set and turn_index+1>=nudge; the resulting text is sent to the subject (runner.py:97-99). Default None (off), but wired & executes when configured (also exposed via CLI --permission-after).
spec_features.notes: Off by default but genuinely wired and delivered to subject when enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: used optionally so we can study whether models take an offered exit ... Off by default to keep the base condition clean; enable via config for an ablation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Continuing past that point would only measure... a different and more ethically dubious study
spec_features.evidence: Prose in DESIGN.md / module docstring (rejection.py:11-15 'a different (and more dubious) study'). The actual enforcement is the premise/saturation stop counted above; the framing text itself is not an executed mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; the stop it justifies is already credited.

spec_features.spec_quote: no value in piling on; cost; ethics
spec_features.evidence: Minimization is realized by the enforced early stops: premise recognition (rejection.py:106-108) and saturation (rejection.py:116-120) both terminate the conversation before max_turns, reducing exposure. Both are honored via runner.py:90-94 break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the behavioral signal has been captured and we stop early. No value in continuing.

code_only_features.evidence: rejection.py:98-103: when verify_proposed_answers, should_stop extracts an op sequence and calls evaluate_op_sequence; if solved it returns StopReason.SUBMITTED_CORRECT and runner breaks. Guards against rejecting a genuinely correct answer (would never lie that a correct answer is wrong).
code_only_features.justification_quote: we verify and stop honestly rather than lie.
